note: Manual readings of bills/ps/<ch>.txt (Private Sector Impact of the final analysis) for the 2013-2020 sessions. b true only when the analysis itself names a kind of business or company that benefits (same test as ../../flhouse/bills/judge.json and scripts/data/state/bills/overrides.json). titleClass: true marks a law judged by its title class (claim bills) without an analysis reading.

2013-2.note: sweepstakes/arcade operators lose sales; burden only

2013-21.note: liability protection for caregivers of children in care (foster parents); not a kind of business

2013-23.note: benefit to private property owners, not a business

2013-26.note: optometrists only bear coursework costs; patients save

2013-27.note: certification companies given a task; no benefit stated

2013-28.cat: design professionals (engineers, surveyors and mappers, architects, landscape architects)
2013-28.q: The design professionals affected by the bill may experience lower costs for professional liability insurance
2013-28.note: limits tort claims against design professionals employed by business entities

2013-31.note: cost savings for ocean-outfall wastewater utilities (local governments) passed to customers; no business named

2013-39.cat: manufacturers (machinery and equipment sales tax exemption)
2013-39.q: By reducing the tax burden of existing manufacturers, the bill may encourage capital investment and new job opportunities in Florida’s manufacturing sector.
2013-39.note: also small businesses via SBDC network

2013-46.note: corporate taxpayers lose near-term bonus depreciation

2013-50.cat: cancer care providers receiving the Quality Cancer Care award
2013-50.q: Providers receiving the award may be able to secure additional patient revenues as a result of the distinction of their care.

2013-60.note: insurer provisions are rate-filing options and Citizens eligibility limits; benefits stated for policyholders

2013-61.cat: property insurers in the Citizens clearinghouse (underwriting records exempt from disclosure)
2013-61.q: Underwriting guidelines, manuals, rating information and other underwriting criteria belonging to insurers participating in the Citizens clearinghouse program will be protected, thereby preventing release of information that could put such insurers at a competitive disadvantage.

2013-66.cat: property and casualty and medical malpractice insurers (rate and form filing exemptions)
2013-66.q: Allowing certain insurers to self-certify their own forms will be more convenient for the industry

2013-68.note: describes costs of a possible EPA hazardous-waste designation, not a benefit from the bill

2013-70.note: general continuity for the private sector; no kind of business named as benefiting

2013-73.cat: noninstructional school contractors (one statewide ID badge)
2013-73.q: This may result in reduced costs for noninstructional contractors.

2019-13.note: savings for clients of lawyers; individuals

2019-19.q: The changes provided by the bill will allow manufacturers to build safer, more comfortable and better performing vehicles.

2019-23.q: The bill provides school districts with additional flexibility for constructing educational facilities, which may lead to additional school construction, benefitting the construction industry.

2019-42.cat: commercial tenants and landlords (lower sales tax on commercial rent)
2019-42.q: The bill will reduce the sales tax on the rental of commercial real estate.
2019-42.note: same reading as 2023-157 and 2025-208 in the other slices

2019-43.cat: construction businesses; freight and logistics businesses (M-CORES corridors)
2019-43.q: Construction businesses may experience improved employee recruitment as a result of the workforce development program.

2019-57.q: The bill may have a positive direct economic impact on the private sector by reducing litigation costs for insurers and lowering insurance rates for consumers.

2019-69.q: In the event of certain crashes, railroad companies may benefit due to reduced delays.

2019-71.cat: online notaries public; businesses that use notaries (remote notarization)
2019-71.q: these businesses and professions may see a reduction in expenditures as a result of allowing this alternative, more convenient method of notarization. Additionally, the bill provides that an online notary public may charge a fee

2019-72.q: TNCs would have the opportunity to compete with existing transportation providers to provide services to Medicaid recipients.

2019-73.cat: motor vehicle and vessel lienholders, including lenders
2019-73.q: The bill may reduce losses experienced by motor vehicle and vessel lienholders, including lenders

2019-75.q: The bill may have a positive economic impact on contractors as a result of the removal of liability for a previous contractor’s work when taking over a construction project.

2019-79.cat: qualified nonprofit housing organization (rental units for prepaid-plan students)
2019-79.q: This bill would benefit a qualified nonprofit organization by providing them with access to a larger pool of potential residents, thereby increasing the revenue generation of their rental units.

2019-82.q: Insurers and consumers will benefit from forms that do not include notices that contradict the actual coverage issued.

2019-83.q: would potentially reduce such assessments for health insurers

2019-84.cat: registered electrical contractors (statewide scope by grandfathering)
2019-84.q: There may be a positive impact on the private sector by expanding the geographical scope of practice for those registered contractors that choose to take advantage of the grandfathering provision.

2019-86.cat: engineering firms (fees removed); non-design-build contractors (more public contracts)
2019-86.q: reduce the costs associated with obtaining a license for an engineering firm

2019-88.cat: aircraft fuel and service providers holding liens; commercial aircraft operators
2019-88.q: This may make it easier for a lienor to recover money owed to him or her without keeping a commercial aircraft out of service

2019-92.cat: independent vehicle storage and title-processing entities
2019-92.q: Independent entities may experience a reduction in costs associated with vehicle storage and transaction processing.

2019-94.q: Other provisions may make it easier for a prevailing contractor to collect attorney fees in a claim against the surety insurer.

2019-99.cat: wholesale drug distributors and pharmacies (drug importation)
2019-99.q: To the extent that such entities participate in the program to import cheaper versions of FDA-approved drugs, they may experience a cost savings.

2019-100.q: insurers could incur lower treatment costs when insureds choose cost-effective treatment options
